blocks.html: Nevertheless, that he shall be confronted with the said du Tilh, prisoner, with Pierre Guerre, Bertrande de Rols and the sisters of the said Martin, together with certain other witnesses who were the principal of those who had so pertinaciously assured that the prisoner was truly Martin Guerre. He is heard; he sets down and gives tokens upon the same interrogations that had been put to the said prisoner — not, however, so certain, so proper, in so great a number, nor of such multitude as the said accused had given. Afterwards he is confronted with the said du Tilh, prisoner, who shows himself more obstinate than ever, calling the said Martin, the newcomer, a cheat, a wicked man, a beggarly knave; submitting himself moreover, under penalty of being hanged, to make good that this newcomer had been bought for ready money and instructed by Pierre Guerre — not, however, so well that he would not confound him and clearly demonstrate the substitution. And upon this he begins to discourse, and to interrogate him about several things that had passed in the house of the said Martin Guerre; whereupon, in truth, the newcomer did not satisfy so well as the prisoner had done, and was still doing.
